title: Fire Emblem's Free Phone Game Is Nintendo's Only Billion-Dollar App
hook:
Fire Emblem Heroes passed $1 billion in player spending in 2022, more than Mario Kart Tour and Pocket Camp combined, and it is still Nintendo's only mobile game to get there. Which hero did your orbs go to?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know a free Fire Emblem phone game is the only Nintendo mobile game to ever pass one billion dollars? In December two thousand sixteen, Nintendo launched Super Mario Run, its first big smartphone game. You downloaded it free and paid ten dollars once to unlock everything. Fire Emblem Heroes arrived just two months after that, at the start of February the following year. It was free to play, and players spent money on orbs to summon heroes from across the series. By October two thousand seventeen, Nintendo's president told investors that Mario Run had passed two hundred million downloads. But he admitted it had not reached an acceptable profit point. Fire Emblem Heroes, he said, was on track to meet its profit goals. The gap only grew from there. Then, in the summer of twenty twenty two, Heroes crossed a billion dollars in lifetime player spending. It is still the only Nintendo mobile game to get there. It has earned more than Mario Kart Tour and Animal Crossing Pocket Camp put together. Around half of that money came from Japan, with the United States second. Mario Kart Tour stopped getting new content a few years ago. Heroes is still running, and it turns ten this coming February. So which Fire Emblem character did you spend your orbs chasing? Follow for more gaming history.
